content: 1. The combination of cefepime and enmetazobactam reduces the efficacy of intravesical live BCG therapy due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. It is recommended to avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Administration of live bacterial vaccines should be delayed until the completion of antibiotic treatment. 2. Cefepime and enmetazobactam decrease the effectiveness of live BCG vaccines through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid co-administration or consider alternative therapies. Live bacterial vaccines should only be administered after completing the antibiotic regimen. 3. Cefepime and enmetazobactam reduce the efficacy of the cholera vaccine due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid co-administration with systemic antibiotics, as these agents may act against the vaccine strain. The cholera vaccine should not be given to patients who have received oral or parenteral antibiotics within 14 days prior to vaccination. 4. The combination of cefepime and enmetazobactam diminishes the effects of oral microbiota products containing bacterial spores due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Antibacterial agents may reduce the efficacy of these products if co-administered. Complete antibiotic regimens 2–4 days before initiating oral microbiota therapy. 5. Cefepime and enmetazobactam reduce the effectiveness of live typhoid vaccines through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative therapies. Live bacterial vaccines should be administered only after completing antibiotic treatment. 6. Cefepime and enmetazobactam increase the toxicity of amikacin, potentially causing nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Use caution and monitor closely. Cephalosporins may enhance the nephrotoxic effects of aminoglycosides. 7. Cefepime and enmetazobactam reduce the efficacy of atezolizumab through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely, as co-administration may interfere with the therapeutic effects of immune checkpoint inhibitors. 8. Cefepime and enmetazobactam reduce the efficacy of avelumab through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely, as co-administration may interfere with the therapeutic effects of immune checkpoint inhibitors. 9. Cefepime and enmetazobactam reduce the efficacy of balstilimab through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely, as co-administration may interfere with the therapeutic effects of immune checkpoint inhibitors. 10. Cefepime and enmetazobactam decrease the levels or effects of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure, but an alternative or additional form of birth control may be advisable during concomitant use. 11. Cefepime and enmetazobactam reduce the efficacy of camrelizumab through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely, as co-administration may interfere with the therapeutic effects of immune checkpoint inhibitors. 12. Cefepime and enmetazobactam reduce the efficacy of cemiplimab through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely, as co-administration may interfere with the therapeutic effects of immune checkpoint inhibitors. 13. Cefepime and enmetazobactam reduce the efficacy of dostarlimab through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely, as co-administration may interfere with the therapeutic effects of immune checkpoint inhibitors. 14. Cefepime and enmetazobactam reduce the efficacy of durvalumab through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely, as co-administration may interfere with the therapeutic effects of immune checkpoint inhibitors. 15. Cefepime and enmetazobactam decrease the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure, but an alternative or additional form of birth control may be advisable during concomitant use. 16. Co-administration of furosemide with cefepime and enmetazobactam may increase the toxicity of either drug, potentially causing nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Use caution and monitor renal function closely. Reports of nephrotoxicity with this combination are inconsistent. 17. Cefepime and enmetazobactam increase the toxicity of gentamicin, potentially causing nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Use caution and monitor closely. Cephalosporins may enhance the nephrotoxic effects of aminoglycosides. 18. Cefepime and enmetazobactam increase the toxicity of kanamycin, potentially causing nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Use caution and monitor closely. Cephalosporins may enhance the nephrotoxic effects of aminoglycosides. 19. Cefepime and enmetazobactam decrease the levels or effects of levonorgestrel/ethinylestradiol/ferrous bisglycinate by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure, but an alternative or additional form of birth control may be advisable during concomitant use. 20. Cefepime and enmetazobactam increase the toxicity of neomycin (oral), potentially causing nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Use caution and monitor closely. Cephalosporins may enhance the nephrotoxic effects of aminoglycosides. 21. Cefepime and enmetazobactam reduce the efficacy of nivolumab through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely, as co-administration may interfere with the therapeutic effects of immune checkpoint inhibitors. 22. Cefepime and enmetazobactam reduce the efficacy of pembrolizumab through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely, as co-administration may interfere with the therapeutic effects of immune checkpoint inhibitors. 23. Cefepime and enmetazobactam reduce the efficacy of penpulimab through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely, as co-administration may interfere with the therapeutic effects of immune checkpoint inhibitors. 24. Cefepime and enmetazobactam increase the toxicity of plazomicin, potentially causing nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Use caution and monitor closely. Cephalosporins may enhance the nephrotoxic effects of aminoglycosides. 25. Probenecid increases the levels or effects of cefepime and enmetazobactam by competing for renal tubular clearance of acidic (anionic) drugs. Use caution and monitor closely. 26. Cefepime and enmetazobactam reduce the efficacy of retifanlimab through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely, as co-administration may interfere with the therapeutic effects of immune checkpoint inhibitors. 27. Cefepime and enmetazobactam reduce the efficacy of sintilimab through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely, as co-administration may interfere with the therapeutic effects of immune checkpoint inhibitors. 28. Cefepime and enmetazobactam decrease the efficacy of sodium picosulfate/magnesium oxide/anhydrous citric acid by altering metabolism. Co-administration with antibiotics reduces efficacy by altering colonic bacterial flora needed to convert sodium picosulfate to its active form. Use caution and monitor closely. 29. Cefepime and enmetazobactam increase the toxicity of streptomycin, potentially causing nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Use caution and monitor closely. Cephalosporins may enhance the nephrotoxic effects of aminoglycosides. 30. Cefepime and enmetazobactam reduce the efficacy of tislelizumab through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely, as co-administration may interfere with the therapeutic effects of immune checkpoint inhibitors. 31. Cefepime and enmetazobactam increase the toxicity of tobramycin, potentially causing nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Use caution and monitor closely. Cephalosporins may enhance the nephrotoxic effects of aminoglycosides. 32. Cefepime and enmetazobactam reduce the efficacy of toripalimab through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely, as co-administration may interfere with the therapeutic effects of immune checkpoint inhibitors. 33. Cefepime and enmetazobactam increase the effects of warfarin through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely, as cefepime/enmetazobactam may decrease prothrombin activity. 34. Cefepime and enmetazobactam increase the levels or effects of aminohippurate sodium by competing for renal tubular clearance of acidic (anionic) drugs. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but close monitoring is advised.
